_notes: DEMO DATA — fictional entries generated for prototype/dev evaluation, not real installations. Matches the schema in installations.json. Swap these out for real entries as they come in — keep the same shape.

installations.name: Corner Rain Garden & Curb Cut
installations.description: A street-facing rain garden fed by a legal curb cut, catching runoff from the block before it reaches the storm drain. Planted in wet-to-dry zones from the curb inward.
installations.visitor_notes: Best viewed from the north side of the street, especially after a rain.

installations.name: Native Slope Restoration
installations.description: A steep front slope converted from turf to a mixed native planting — coast live oak, sagebrush, and monkeyflower — reducing both watering needs and erosion risk.
installations.visitor_notes: Visible year-round; spring bloom is the most dramatic time to visit.

installations.name: Rain Barrel + Drip Integration
installations.description: Two connected rain barrels feed a gravity-fed drip line to a native planting bed, professionally installed as part of a broader landscape renovation.
installations.visitor_notes: Barrels are visible from the driveway side; ring the bell for a look at the drip system.

installations.name: Parkway Swale Garden
installations.description: A shallow parkway swale installed by a small group of neighbors on the same block, coordinating water flow across three adjoining properties.
installations.visitor_notes: Ask about the block's shared maintenance schedule if you're curious how coordination works.

installations.name: Food Forest Front Yard
installations.description: A full front-yard conversion combining native plants with food-bearing species suited to the region, including a mature guava and prickly pear.
installations.visitor_notes: Fruit is for the birds, not for picking — please admire from the sidewalk.

installations.name: City Park Bioswale Demonstration
installations.description: A city-installed demonstration bioswale at the edge of a public park, with signage explaining how it captures and filters street runoff.
installations.visitor_notes: Interpretive signage on site — a good first stop if you're new to the concept.

installations.name: Curb Cut & Dry Creek Bed
installations.description: A decorative dry creek bed channels curb-cut runoff across the length of the front yard before it infiltrates near the property line.
installations.visitor_notes: The creek bed is most active during and right after rain.

installations.name: Mulch Basin & Native Meadow
installations.description: Shallow mulch basins around existing trees paired with a low native meadow mix replacing what was previously lawn.
installations.visitor_notes: Meadow is left uncut through spring for pollinators.
